title: ClarkAtlanta vs FAMU: control, tuition, size
summary: Clark Atlanta University (ClarkAtlanta) versus Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (FAMU). Also searched as FAMU vs ClarkAtlanta. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Clark Atlanta University and Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (ClarkAtlanta vs FAMU) differ primarily in ownership and size. Clark Atlanta is a private nonprofit institution located in Atlanta, while FAMU is a public university based in Tallahassee. The undergraduate enrollment at Clark Atlanta is 3,603 students, compared to FAMU's larger undergraduate population of 7,582. Tuition costs also vary significantly, with Clark Atlanta charging $28,310 for in-state students, whereas FAMU's in-state tuition is $5,785. These distinctions highlight differences in governance, scale, and cost between ClarkAtlanta vs FAMU.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: When comparing Clark Atlanta University and Florida Agricultural and Mechanical University (ClarkAtlanta vs FAMU), notable differences in cost emerge. Clark Atlanta University, a private institution, charges $28,310 for both in-state and out-of-state tuition. In contrast, FAMU, a public university, has a lower tuition rate of $5,785 for in-state students and $17,725 for out-of-state students. Regarding student debt, the median debt for graduates of Clark Atlanta is $27,000, while FAMU graduates have a slightly lower median debt of $23,548. These figures illustrate the financial considerations prospective students might weigh when choosing between ClarkAtlanta vs FAMU.
